title: Sentient Foundation Launches Open Benchmark to Prove AI Model Ownership
summary:
The Fingerprinting Leaderboard, a free open-source tool, evaluates the ability of AI developers to embed ownership marks within model weights to detect unauthorized duplication. Sentient Foundation's new benchmark, and its accompanying mlprints code, tests how these fingerprints resist removal attempts such as distillation or fine-tuning while preserving original model performance. Researchers submit marking methods, which are then embedded into test models and ranked on a public website based on verification reliability and resilience.

AI models often cost millions to train but can be copied in minutes, creating a need for proof of ownership that resides in the weights rather than in paperwork. Fingerprinting achieves this by training a model to provide unlikely answers to secret prompts, allowing owners to verify suspected copies through an API. Sentient's own Perinucleus method is currently competing on the leaderboard after embedding 24,576 fingerprints in Llama-3.1-8B without degrading the model's utility.

selectedTweets.text:
Good news for anyone trying to prove a model is theirs.

Sentient Foundation released the Fingerprinting Leaderboard, a free, open source benchmark that tests fingerprinting methods, meant to prove an AI model was copied from yours.

Researchers submit a method for hiding an ownership mark inside a model, and Sentient puts that mark into its own test models, tries to strip it out, then ranks the method on a public website.

The code that runs these tests, called mlprints, is released too.

A fingerprint trains a model to return unlikely answers to secret prompts, so an owner can test a suspected copy through its API alone. 

But a fingerprint that survives every attack is still useless if the owner can’t read it back reliably.

Sentient Foundation’s Fingerprinting Leaderboard scores that verification step directly, alongside how well the mark resists removal and how much model skill it costs.

Sentient’s Perinucleus method embedded 24,576 fingerprints in Llama-3.1-8B without degrading utility, is also competing on the leaderboard, and the fingerprints survived standard fine-tuning.
